subject.name: Physics I: Mechanics
subject.description: Calculus-based mechanics for first-year engineering: kinematics, Newton's laws, energy and momentum, rotation, gravitation, and oscillations. The foundation for all later engineering physics.

depth_levels.awareness: Know it exists and recognize it
depth_levels.procedural: Apply it mechanically to standard problems
depth_levels.fluency: Combine it with other tools in multi-step problems
depth_levels.proof: State it precisely and derive or prove it

topics.name: Measurement, Units, and Vectors
topics.description: The mathematical toolkit the whole course runs on: units, uncertainty, and vector algebra.

subtopics.name: SI units and dimensional analysis
subtopics.description: Base and derived SI units; checking equations with dimensional analysis; unit conversion.

subtopics.name: Significant figures and measurement uncertainty
subtopics.description: Reporting results to the right precision; propagating simple uncertainties.

subtopics.name: Scalars versus vectors
subtopics.description: What makes a quantity a vector; magnitude and direction.

subtopics.name: Resolving vectors into components
subtopics.description: Breaking a vector into x, y, z components and rebuilding it.

subtopics.name: Unit vectors and i, j, k notation
subtopics.description: Writing vectors in component (unit-vector) form.

subtopics.name: Vector addition and subtraction
subtopics.description: Graphical (tip-to-tail) and component methods for combining vectors.

subtopics.name: The scalar (dot) product
subtopics.description: Computing A·B; using it for angles and projections.

subtopics.name: The vector (cross) product and the right-hand rule
subtopics.description: Computing A×B; direction via the right-hand rule.

subtopics.name: Coordinate systems
subtopics.description: Cartesian and polar coordinates and when each is convenient.

topics.name: Kinematics in One Dimension
topics.description: Describing straight-line motion with position, velocity, and acceleration.

subtopics.name: Position, displacement, and distance
subtopics.description: Displacement as a vector versus total distance travelled.

subtopics.name: Average velocity and average speed
subtopics.description: The difference between average velocity and average speed.

subtopics.name: Instantaneous velocity as a derivative
subtopics.description: Velocity as the derivative of position with respect to time.

subtopics.name: Acceleration in one dimension
subtopics.description: Average and instantaneous acceleration; sign conventions.

subtopics.name: Kinematic equations for constant acceleration
subtopics.description: The constant-acceleration (SUVAT) equations and choosing which to use.

subtopics.name: Free fall under gravity
subtopics.description: Vertical motion with g; symmetry of the trajectory.

subtopics.name: Interpreting motion graphs
subtopics.description: Reading slopes and areas of x–t, v–t, and a–t graphs.

subtopics.name: Kinematics with calculus
subtopics.description: Getting velocity and position by integrating acceleration.

topics.name: Kinematics in Two and Three Dimensions
topics.description: Motion in a plane and in space, using vectors.

subtopics.name: Position and velocity vectors
subtopics.description: Describing motion in 2D/3D with vector position and velocity.

subtopics.name: The acceleration vector
subtopics.description: Acceleration as a vector; its components along and perpendicular to velocity.

subtopics.name: Projectile motion
subtopics.description: Independent horizontal and vertical motion under gravity.

subtopics.name: Range, maximum height, and the trajectory equation
subtopics.description: Deriving range and height; the parabolic path equation.

subtopics.name: Uniform circular motion and centripetal acceleration
subtopics.description: Why circular motion is accelerated; a = v²/r toward the center.

subtopics.name: Non-uniform circular motion
subtopics.description: Splitting acceleration into radial and tangential parts.

subtopics.name: Relative velocity and reference frames
subtopics.description: Transforming velocities between moving reference frames.

topics.name: Newton's Laws of Motion
topics.description: The link between force and motion — the core of dynamics.

subtopics.name: Newton's first law and inertia
subtopics.description: Inertia and the idea of an inertial reference frame.

subtopics.name: Force as a vector
subtopics.description: Forces, their units, and combining them as vectors.

subtopics.name: Newton's second law (F = ma)
subtopics.description: Net force, mass, and acceleration; component form of the second law.

subtopics.name: Mass versus weight
subtopics.description: The distinction between mass and gravitational weight.

subtopics.name: Newton's third law and action–reaction pairs
subtopics.description: Identifying correct action–reaction pairs.

subtopics.name: Drawing free-body diagrams
subtopics.description: Isolating an object and drawing every force acting on it.

subtopics.name: Normal, tension, and other contact forces
subtopics.description: Modeling surfaces, strings, and supports as forces.

subtopics.name: Solving Newton's-law problems
subtopics.description: Setting up and solving systems of equations from free-body diagrams.

topics.name: Applications of Newton's Laws
topics.description: Friction, drag, and circular dynamics — Newton's laws in real situations.

subtopics.name: Static friction
subtopics.description: The maximum-static-friction model and impending motion.

subtopics.name: Kinetic friction
subtopics.description: Friction on a sliding surface; the coefficient of kinetic friction.

subtopics.name: Inclined-plane problems
subtopics.description: Choosing tilted axes; motion on ramps with and without friction.

subtopics.name: Drag forces and terminal velocity
subtopics.description: Velocity-dependent resistive forces; reaching terminal velocity.

subtopics.name: Dynamics of circular motion (centripetal force)
subtopics.description: Applying F = ma to circular motion; what provides the centripetal force.

subtopics.name: Banked curves
subtopics.description: Circular motion on a banked track, with and without friction.

subtopics.name: Connected objects and pulleys
subtopics.description: Atwood machines and coupled systems with constraints.

subtopics.name: Work done by a constant force
subtopics.description: W = F·d as a dot product; positive, negative, and zero work.

subtopics.name: Work done by a variable force
subtopics.description: Work as the integral of force over displacement.

subtopics.name: The work–energy theorem
subtopics.description: Net work equals the change in kinetic energy.

subtopics.name: Kinetic energy
subtopics.description: The definition ½mv² and its units.

subtopics.name: Power
subtopics.description: Average and instantaneous power; P = F·v.

subtopics.name: Work done by a spring (Hooke's law)
subtopics.description: Force and work for an ideal spring.

topics.name: Potential Energy and Conservation of Energy
topics.description: Storing energy and tracking it through a process.

subtopics.name: Conservative versus non-conservative forces
subtopics.description: Path-independence and what defines a conservative force.

subtopics.name: Gravitational potential energy (near Earth)
subtopics.description: U = mgy and choice of reference level.

subtopics.name: Elastic potential energy
subtopics.description: The ½kx² energy stored in a spring.

subtopics.name: Conservation of mechanical energy
subtopics.description: Trading kinetic and potential energy when only conservative forces act.

subtopics.name: Energy with friction and other losses
subtopics.description: Accounting for energy dissipated by non-conservative forces.

subtopics.name: Force as the gradient of potential energy
subtopics.description: Recovering force from U via F = −dU/dx.

subtopics.name: Energy diagrams and equilibrium
subtopics.description: Reading potential-energy curves; stable and unstable equilibria.

topics.name: Momentum, Impulse, and Collisions
topics.description: The momentum view, and what stays constant in interactions.

subtopics.name: Linear momentum
subtopics.description: The definition p = mv as a vector quantity.

subtopics.name: Impulse and the impulse–momentum theorem
subtopics.description: Impulse as the integral of force; its equality with the change in momentum.

subtopics.name: Conservation of momentum
subtopics.description: Why total momentum is conserved for an isolated system.

subtopics.name: Elastic collisions
subtopics.description: Collisions conserving both momentum and kinetic energy.

subtopics.name: Inelastic and perfectly inelastic collisions
subtopics.description: Momentum conserved, kinetic energy lost; objects sticking together.

subtopics.name: Collisions in two dimensions
subtopics.description: Applying momentum conservation component-by-component.

subtopics.name: Center of mass
subtopics.description: Locating the center of mass of particles and continuous bodies.

subtopics.name: Motion of the center of mass
subtopics.description: The center of mass moves as if all mass and net external force acted there.

subtopics.name: Systems of variable mass (rockets)
subtopics.description: The rocket equation and thrust from ejected mass.

topics.name: Rotational Motion
topics.description: Rotation of rigid bodies: kinematics, inertia, torque, and energy.

subtopics.name: Angular position, velocity, and acceleration
subtopics.description: Rotational analogues of linear kinematic quantities.

subtopics.name: Rotational kinematic equations
subtopics.description: Constant-angular-acceleration equations.

subtopics.name: Relating linear and angular quantities
subtopics.description: v = rω and a = rα for points on a rotating body.

subtopics.name: Moment of inertia
subtopics.description: Rotational inertia and its dependence on the axis.

subtopics.name: The parallel-axis theorem
subtopics.description: Shifting the moment of inertia to a parallel axis.

subtopics.name: Calculating moments of inertia by integration
subtopics.description: Integrating r²dm for rods, disks, and spheres.

subtopics.name: Torque
subtopics.description: Torque as r×F; moment arm and sign.

subtopics.name: Newton's second law for rotation (τ = Iα)
subtopics.description: The rotational analogue of F = ma.

subtopics.name: Rotational kinetic energy
subtopics.description: ½Iω² and energy methods for rotation.

subtopics.name: Rolling without slipping
subtopics.description: Combining translation and rotation; the rolling constraint.

subtopics.name: Work and power in rotation
subtopics.description: Work done by a torque and rotational power.

topics.name: Angular Momentum and Static Equilibrium
topics.description: Conservation of angular momentum, and the conditions for a body at rest.

subtopics.name: Angular momentum of a particle
subtopics.description: L = r×p and its dependence on the reference point.

subtopics.name: Angular momentum of a rigid body
subtopics.description: L = Iω for rotation about a fixed axis.

subtopics.name: Torque and the rate of change of angular momentum
subtopics.description: Deriving τ = dL/dt.

subtopics.name: Conservation of angular momentum
subtopics.description: Why L is conserved with no net external torque; the spinning-skater effect.

subtopics.name: Gyroscopes and precession
subtopics.description: Qualitative precession of a spinning top.

subtopics.name: Conditions for static equilibrium
subtopics.description: Zero net force and zero net torque together.

subtopics.name: Center of gravity
subtopics.description: Where gravity effectively acts; relation to center of mass.

subtopics.name: Solving equilibrium problems (beams, ladders)
subtopics.description: Choosing a pivot and solving rigid-body statics.

subtopics.name: Stress, strain, and elasticity

topics.name: Gravitation

subtopics.description: The inverse-square gravitational force between masses.

subtopics.name: Gravitational field and g

subtopics.name: Escape velocity

subtopics.name: Energy in orbits
subtopics.description: Total mechanical energy of bound orbits and its sign.

topics.name: Oscillations (Simple Harmonic Motion)

subtopics.description: Deriving and solving x'' = −ω²x.

subtopics.name: Energy in simple harmonic motion

subtopics.description: Small-angle SHM of a pendulum and its period.

subtopics.description: Oscillation of an extended body about a pivot.

subtopics.description: How damping reduces amplitude over time.

subtopics.name: Driven oscillations and resonance
subtopics.description: Response to a periodic driving force and resonance.
